findings.title: Delete action missing from alert list view
findings.body: The condition `{canDelete && rulerRule && (` requires `rulerRule` to be truthy. In the new alert list view, `GrafanaRuleListItem` passes only `promRule` to `RuleActionsButtons`, so `rulerRule` is always `undefined`. Even though `canDelete` is correctly computed as true using `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, the Delete menu item will never render, making it impossible for users to delete Grafana-managed rules from the alert list. This is a regression from the previous behavior where the ruler rule was always available.

findings.title: Pause action missing from alert list view
findings.body: The condition `{canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && groupIdentifier.groupOrigin === 'grafana' && (` depends on `rulerRule`. In the new alert list view, `rulerRule` is `undefined` because only `promRule` is provided. Consequently, even when `canPause` is true via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, the Pause menu item is never shown, preventing users from pausing/unpausing Grafana-managed rules from the list.

findings.title: Federated rule groups become editable/deletable
findings.body: The deprecated `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` and no longer checks `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`. The new implementation sets `isFederated = false` unconditionally (line 244). This means for external (e.g., Mimir) federated rule groups, actions like Update and Delete will be reported as supported and allowed, potentially allowing users to edit or delete federated rules that should be immutable. This is a security/authorization regression for components that still use `useAlertRuleAbility`.

findings.title: List view still invokes ruler ability hook with undefined rule
findings.body: `RuleActionsButtons` always calls `useRulerRuleAbility(rule, groupIdentifier, AlertRuleAction.Update)` even when `rule` (RulerRuleDTO) is `undefined` in the new list view. This hook eventually calls `useIsRuleEditable(rulesSourceName, undefined)`, which may still trigger ruler API requests (e.g., to determine ruler availability). Since the PR aims to remove all ruler API requests from the alert list, this undermines the performance improvement. Consider using a skip mechanism for the ruler hook when only `promRule` is available.
